ux.why: V2 gives one focal point (a single store select and Connect store, then "Step 1 of 2"/"Step 2 of 2" with Finish setup disabled and the tooltip "Choose a location first."), while V1 opens on an alert, three identical "Connect store" buttons and empty Activity/Sync blocks ("Held –", "Enable") all at the same time.

accountant.why: V1 shows every requirement for a store on its card in precise wording ("change Created product should be from Non-inventory to Inventory", plus "1 item needs mapping"), while V2's step header "Enable inventory tracking" mixes up the QuickBooks product-type setting with Shopify's own quantity tracking and leaves mapping out of setup.

business_owner.why: "Start with one store. You can connect the others later." and "After connecting, 2 short steps get the store ready." set a small, safe scope; V1 shows status words like Held/Failed and a disabled-state Sync block before the user has done anything.

ux.why: The wide stores column (764px vs 435px) shortens the store card that needs setup from 1082px to 862px tall, and the clickable tiles with chevrons read as one row; the cost is that in setup state the top line is four "–" tiles placed above the Enable button.

accountant.why: V1's Activity block defines every status on hover ("Held: Not sent. Fix the reason, then click Retry.", "Applied in 24h: Sent. The stock in Shopify was updated."); the V2 state map records "no tooltips on tiles", so Held/Failed/Pending have no definitions.

business_owner.why: A first-timer who sees "Held 1" can hover in V1 and learn what to do ("Fix the reason, then click Retry"); in V2 the same bare number has no explanation, and that is an anxiety trigger.

ux.why: V2 lands straight on the work (rows with "Update Shopify qty / Ignore", Store filter, "Unresolved only", select all → "2 selected"), while V1 makes the user pick a row in a run log and click "View rows" for each store before they can act.

accountant.why: The bulk dialog still names each amount and its source ("as found in the latest comparison of My ceramic plates on Oct 2, 2026 02:30: Ceramic plate 24cm: +8, Mug set: +2"), the audit trail stays under "Previous comparisons (4)" → View rows, and a failed run is stated on the page ("My good flowers: failed Oct 2, 2026 02:30"). This also saves the per-store clicks that add up across 40+ clients.

business_owner.why: "Only products that differ are listed" and an immediate list of differences answer "what do I fix?"; V1's table of runs ("Trigger / Items compared / Differences 0") asks the owner to understand comparisons first.

ux.why: V2 wins all three areas on focus and fewer steps. The one UX debt it adds is two setup models: a 2-step wizard for the first store and a 3-step card in a different order for later stores.

accountant.why: Precise setup wording and defined statuses matter more to an accountant than click count. V1 loses only the Stock check tab, and that part could be moved over.

business_owner.why: The small scoped start and the differences-first Stock check remove the two biggest quit-risk moments. V2's one regression is the unexplained tiles.

hybrid.combination: V2 empty state + onboarding, V2 Overview layout, V2 Stock check tab. Add two V1 pieces: the V1 Activity status tooltips on the four top-line tiles, and the V1 step wording "Set Created product to Inventory" (from Non-inventory to Inventory) in place of "Enable inventory tracking" in onboarding step 1.
hybrid.why: This keeps V2's focus and cross-store bulk, which win UX and Business owner, and fixes the only two points where the accountant lens prefers V1. Both fixes are copy/tooltip moves, not layout changes.

V1: First setup has competing focal points: an info alert, three "Connect store" buttons, and empty Activity/Stock check/Sync blocks are all visible before any store exists.
In the 435px stores column, a card that needs setup grows to 918-1082px tall and pushes other stores below the fold.
The Stock check tab is a run log: with differences in several stores the user has to open each comparison separately, and there is no cross-store bulk action.
The store-missing hint differs between the connect dialog ("Add it first in Settings › Add integration.") and the card footer ("Connect it first in Organization settings").
V2: There are two setup models: the first store uses a wizard (inventory, then location, no mapping), later stores use the card's 3 numbered steps (location, inventory, mapping) in a different order.
The top-line tiles have no tooltips, so Held/Failed/Pending are undefined numbers.
After Finish setup, the next required action (Enable) is signalled only by a toast and sits in the narrow left column under four "–" tiles (KF-2 risk).

Gap: the cross-store bulk "Update Shopify qty" dialog was only exercised with one store's differences, so it is unknown whether it groups amounts by store and comparison date when several stores are selected.
A failed nightly check appears only as inline text in the "Latest comparison" line, which is easy to miss next to "No unresolved differences."
